policy_presence.summary: The University of Melbourne distributes AI policy across Subject Coordinator instructions, the Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310), the Responsible Conduct of Research Policy framework (MPF1318 consultation memorandum), and the University AI Principles.

ai_disclosure.summary: University of Melbourne guidance requires citing AI outputs in the reference list when quoting or paraphrasing, and providing an acknowledgement declaration at the end of the assessment for other process assistance such as brainstorming, planning, or editing.

coursework.summary: At the University of Melbourne, each Subject Coordinator sets the boundaries of appropriate GenAI use in their subject; students must check before using AI for assessment-related work and produce the submitted work themselves unless explicitly authorized.

exams.summary: Public evidence is insufficient to establish an affirmative University-wide GenAI permission for examinations. Under University guidelines on assuring learning against GenAI circumvention, in most cases subjects are designed so that secure assessments (such as invigilated exams) account for at least 50% of subject marks (phased 2026–2028); specific exam rules are set by subject coordinators, unauthorized or undisclosed AI use constitutes misconduct under MPF1310, and tool access conveys no exam permission.

privacy_data_entry.summary: Students and researchers must not upload full names, dates of birth, addresses, confidential, sensitive or private information, or third-party copyright materials into GenAI tools. University IP must not be uploaded to external platforms; SparkAI is recommended for internal staff materials review.

academic_integrity.summary: Under MPF1310, unauthorised or undisclosed technology use in assessable work constitutes misconduct. Poor Academic Practice is distinguished as non-punitive educative resolution, distinct from Level 1 Faculty-level misconduct and Level 2 Serious Misconduct. Turnitin AI detection reports serve as an investigative prompt rather than proof, and MPF1323 provides a 20-business-day appeal window.

approved_tools.summary: The University of Melbourne provides AILA within Canvas LMS where enabled by coordinators, SparkAI for staff handling sensitive University information, and M365 Copilot Chat for students with private OneDrive storage. Institutional licensing does not convey coursework or examination permission.

named_ai_services.summary: The University of Melbourne provides AILA within Canvas LMS where enabled by coordinators, SparkAI for staff handling sensitive University information, and M365 Copilot Chat for students with private OneDrive storage. Institutional licensing does not convey coursework or examination permission.

teaching_guidance.summary: Melbourne teaching guidelines advise staff to set clear subject AI boundaries, model transparency in teaching materials, and ensure AI tools never replace evaluative academic judgment in marking or grading.

research_guidance.summary: Under institutional research guidance and the Australian Code for the Responsible Conduct of Research, researchers must acknowledge material generated or altered by GenAI, protect confidential or patentable IP from AI prompts, and consult Research Ethics and Integrity DAT guidelines; revised MPF1318 policy proposals introduce explicit DAT expectations.

security_procurement.summary: The University of Melbourne AI Principles establish an overarching framework across literacy, fairness, privacy, and security; staff testing of assessment materials must remain within SparkAI or sanctioned platforms rather than public consumer services.
